chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about semen that hits the garment. He said: If you know its place, wash it, and if its place is hidden from you, wash the whole garment.

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: The garment or clothing, the object of the purity ruling.
key_terms.الْمَنِيِّ: Semen, the fluid emitted during sexual arousal or climax, considered a major impurity (najis) in Shia jurisprudence.
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: So wash it, the imperative command for performing the act of washing (ghasl) to remove impurity.
key_terms.كُلَّهُ: All of it, referring to the entire garment when the specific location of the impurity is unknown.

ai.seo_question: How to wash clothes stained with semen according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-ghalabah* (preponderance) in ritual purity, distinguishing between localized and diffuse impurities. It reflects the Shia juristic preference for ease (*taysir*) by limiting washing to the known stain unless uncertainty prevails, a ruling that underpins the methodology of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in fiqh. This specific guidance highlights the practical application of distinguishing between *najis* (impure) and *tahir* (pure) states in daily worship.
